# School of Math (SOMATH) — full site index

> Complete inventory of every course page, blog post, and guide on schoolofmath.us. Content is organized for LLMs to browse: each link is annotated with a short description drawn from the page's meta description.

For the curated overview, see [llms.txt](https://www.schoolofmath.us/llms.txt).

## Core pages

- [Home](https://www.schoolofmath.us/): NYC math school for grades 1–12. Small groups of 6, Harvard- & Kellogg-trained teachers, free 60-min evaluation. Upper West Side · 226 W 79th St.
- [About SOMATH](https://www.schoolofmath.us/about): Meet Vivianne Wright (Harvard) and Marcelo Ambrozio (Northwestern) — the educators behind School of Math on the Upper West Side. 20 years preparing GMAT/GRE candidates for top business schools. Now teaching grades 1–12.
- [All courses](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses): Browse every SOMATH course — Little Newtons, Kid Einsteins, Young Fermats Pre-Algebra, Algebra Ignite, Geometry, Algebra II, SHSAT Prep, SAT Math, and AP Prep. Pick a day and enroll.
- [Contact](https://www.schoolofmath.us/contact): Visit School of Math at 226 West 79th Street, Upper West Side, NYC. Steps from the 1, B, C trains. Open Mon–Fri 3–10pm, Sat 10am–6pm. Call (646) 668-6151.

## AP Calculus

- [AP Pre-Calc Rational Function: Where Is h(x) > 0?](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/ap-calc-rational-function-positive-intervals-solved): Step-by-step solution to a classic AP Pre-Calculus rational function inequality: factor f(x) = x³ − 3x² − 10x and g(x) = x² − 6x + 5, then use a sign chart to find where h(x) = f(x)/g(x) is positive. Includes video walkthrough.
- [AP Calculus AB vs BC: Which Should Your Child Take?](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/ap-calculus-ab-vs-bc-which-should-my-child-take): A 20-year math teacher explains the real difference between AP Calculus AB and BC, what colleges actually want, the pace trap, and when AB is the right call.

- [Mastering Limits in AP Pre Calculus Limits: Key Strateg…](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/mastering-limits-in-ap-pre-calculus-limits-key-strategies-for-exam-success): Mastering limits is key to success in AP Pre-Calculus. This post covers strategies for understanding end behavior and exponential functions for the AP exam.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q3: Expand & Simplify](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-expand-and-simplify-stewart-problem-3): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 3 — five expansions worked step by step. 3(x+6)+4(2x−5), FOIL on (x+3)(4x−5), the conjugate radical (√a+√b)(√a−√b), the perfect-square binomial (2x+3)², and the cube (x+2)³ — taught the way we teach them at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q1: Exponent Rules Without a Calculator](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-exponent-rules-evaluate-without-calculator): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test A, Problem 1 — six exponent expressions evaluated without a calculator. The (−3)⁴ vs −3⁴ trap, the quotient rule, negative and fractional exponents (16^(−3/4)), explained the way we teach it at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q4: Factor Each Expression](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-factor-each-expression-stewart-problem-4): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 4 — six factoring techniques worked step by step. Difference of squares, trinomial reverse-FOIL, factoring by grouping, sum of cubes, factoring with negative fractional exponents, and two-variable factoring — taught the way we teach them at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q6: Rationalize the Expression](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-rationalize-the-expression-stewart-problem-6): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 6 — two rationalize-the-expression problems worked step by step. Multiply by the conjugate to clear a radical denominator √10/(√5−2), and rationalize the numerator on (√(4+h) − 2)/h — the classic AP Calculus derivative-from-the-definition setup. Taught the way we teach it at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q7: Complete the Square](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-rewrite-by-completing-the-square-stewart-problem-7): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 7 — two complete-the-square problems worked step by step. Rewrite x² + x + 1 into vertex form with a fractional half-coefficient, and 2x² − 12x + 11 with a leading coefficient that has to be factored out first. Taught the way we teach it at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q2: Simplify Radicals & Exponents](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-simplify-radicals-exponents-stewart-problem-2): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 2 — three expressions simplified without negative exponents. √200 − √32 = 6√2, (3a³b³)(4ab²)² = 48a⁵b⁷, and the (3x^(3/2)y³ / x²y^(−1/2))^(−2) = x/9y⁷ — worked the way we teach them at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q5: Simplify Rational Expressions](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-simplify-rational-expressions-stewart-problem-5): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 5 — four rational-expression simplifications worked step by step. Factor and cancel, multiply by reciprocal, subtract with a common denominator, and reduce a complex fraction in two variables — taught the way we teach them at SOMATH, pre-calculus tutoring on the Upper West Side.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q9: Inequality in Interval Notation](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-solve-each-inequality-stewart-problem-9): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 9 — five inequalities, five different techniques, every answer in clean interval notation. Linear with a sign flip, quadratic by factoring and sign chart, higher-degree product, absolute value, and a rational inequality with a critical-point and domain check. The one big-picture lesson every pre-calc student needs before AP Calc.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q8: Solve the Equation (7 Techniques)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-solve-the-equation-stewart-problem-8): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 8 — seven equations, seven different solving techniques worked side by side. Linear, rational with a domain check, factorable quadratic, quadratic formula, quartic-via-substitution, absolute value split, and a negative fractional exponent. The one big-picture lesson every pre-calc student needs before AP Calc.
- [Pre-Calc Diagnostic Q10: State True or False](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/precalc-diagnostic-state-true-or-false-stewart-problem-10): Stewart Pre-Calculus Diagnostic Test, Problem 10 — six algebraic identities, true or false. The six most-tested misconceptions in pre-calc algebra: (p+q)², √(ab), √(a²+b²), splitting sums over a denominator, splitting a fraction across subtraction, and complex fractions. Counter-examples for the false ones, the underlying property for the true ones.
- [Understanding Change of Rate Graphs in AP Pre-Calculus](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/understanding-change-of-rate-graphs-in-ap-pre-calculus): Unlock the secrets of pre calculus rate of change with our in-depth guide. Master pre calculus rate of change concepts for AP Pre-Calculus success.

## Regents Geometry

- [Regents Geometry June 2026 — Part I Answers & Explanations (Questions 1–24)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/regents-geometry-june-2026-part-1-answers): Every Part I question from the June 2026 NYS Geometry Regents exam with click-to-reveal answers, worked solutions, and the theorem behind each one. Original NYSED PDF attached. Covers rigid motions, midsegment theorem, right-triangle trigonometry (co-function, geometric mean altitude), circles (standard form, arc length, tangent-secant power of a point), coordinate geometry (partitioning, dilations of lines), 3D solids (rotating a right triangle to make a cone, cross-sections of a rectangular prism), triangle inequality, and rhombus/parallelogram tests. First of a four-post series covering all 35 questions across Parts I–IV. Prepared by SOMATH — School of Math, an Upper West Side math school. Free download of the original NYSED PDF at /assets/regents/geometry-june-2026/nysed-geometry-june-2026.pdf.
- [Regents Geometry June 2026 — Part II Answers & Explanations (Questions 25–31)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/regents-geometry-june-2026-part-2-answers): Every 2-credit Part II short-answer question from the June 2026 NYS Geometry Regents, worked step-by-step with the theorem behind each one. Covers rigid-motion sequences (Q25 — reflection over the y-axis then translate 1 left/8 down maps DAN to MIK), parallelogram alternate-interior angles and linear pairs (Q26 — angle CSA = 111°), cylinder volume and density (Q27 — 353 lb), converse of the side-splitter theorem (Q28 — FD = 48), the SAS trig area formula ½ab·sin(C) (Q29 — 32.7 sq units), the angle-bisector construction with compass and straightedge (Q30), and the diagonals-congruent rectangle test (Q31 — RM = 2·RP = 24 = GA, so GRAM is a rectangle). Includes rubric notes for full 2-credit answers. Prepared by SOMATH — School of Math, an Upper West Side math school.

## Analytic geometry & functions

- [Analytic Geometry Q3 (Stewart 9e): Circle Center & Radius](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/analytic-geometry-circle-stewart-calculus): Stewart Calculus 9th Edition diagnostic test, analytic geometry Problem 3 — find the center and radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 10y + 9 = 0. Complete the square step by step, rewrite in standard form, and read off center (3, -5) and radius 5. Worked from SOMATH on the Upper West Side.
- [Analytic Geometry Q1 (Stewart 9e): Equation of a Line](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/analytic-geometry-diagnostic-stewart-calculus): Stewart Calculus 9th Edition diagnostic test, analytic geometry Problem 1 — find the equation of a line through (2, -5) under four conditions: slope -3, parallel to the x-axis, parallel to the y-axis, parallel to 2x - 4y = 3. Worked step by step from SOMATH on the Upper West Side.
- [Equation of a Circle from Center & Point (Stewart 9e Q2)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/circle-equation-from-center-and-point-stewart-calculus): Stewart Calculus 9th Edition diagnostic test, analytic geometry Problem 2 — find the equation of the circle with center (-1, 4) that passes through (3, -2). Standard form, distance-formula shortcut, and the final answer (x+1)^2 + (y-4)^2 = 52. Worked from SOMATH on the Upper West Side.
- [Coordinate Geometry: Line, Midpoint & Circle (Ch.1 Q4)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/coordinate-geometry-points-line-circle-stewart-q4): Stewart Calculus 9th Edition diagnostic Q4 — given A(-7, 4) and B(5, -12), find the slope, line equation, intercepts, midpoint, distance, perpendicular bisector, and the equation of the circle with AB as a diameter. Answer (x+1)^2 + (y+4)^2 = 100. Worked from SOMATH on the Upper West Side.
- [Difference Quotient of f(x) = x³ at x = 2 (Ch.1 Q2)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/difference-quotient-x-cubed-stewart-ch1-q2): Stewart Calculus Chapter 1, Question 2 — evaluate the difference quotient [f(2+h) − f(2)] / h for f(x) = x³ and simplify. Answer: h² + 6h + 12. Step-by-step walkthrough with the binomial expansion of (2+h)³, the algebra of cancelling h, and the link to f′(2) = 12. From SOMATH on the Upper West Side.
- [Reading a Function from Its Graph (Stewart Ch.1 Q1)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/reading-function-graph-domain-range-stewart-ch1-q1): Stewart Calculus Chapter 1, Question 1 — read function values, solve f(x) = 2, estimate zeros, and state the domain and range from a graph. f(-1) = -2, f(2) ≈ 2.8, x = -3 and 1 for f(x) = 2, zeros near -2.3 and 0.3, domain [-3, 3], range [-2, 3]. Worked from SOMATH on the Upper West Side.
